summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with end-stage multiple myeloma, COPD, CHF, and a neobladder, was admitted with altered mental status and somnolence. Evaluation revealed an Enterococcus urinary tract infection, hypercalcemia, and silent aspiration confirmed by videofluoroscopy. Despite treatment with vancomycin, pamidronate, and supportive care, his condition deteriorated due to progressive myeloma, worsening renal function, and aspiration pneumonia. A decision was made to transition to comfort-focused care, and he passed peacefully surrounded by family. The hospital course was marked by multidisciplinary support, including palliative care, speech and swallow evaluation, and infection management.
